rows.report: my internet is so slow lately, like videos keep buffering every few seconds and i swear nobody else is using it but maybe the kids are downloading something on their tablets idk how to check what's eating all the speed
hey so netflix keeps freezing on the smart tv and my wife says its been like this all week, is there a way to see whos hogging the wifi? i'm not super techy sorry

getting that not secure warning on my bank website again, the little lock icon has a red line through it and chrome says connection is not private, this happen before but i forgot what i did to fix it

so i went to pay my credit card bill and the browser gave me a big scary warning about the certificate or whatever, said something about it expiring? i just want to make sure its actually my bank and not some fake site

how many things are actually connected to my wifi right now? i see like 15 devices in the router app but i only count maybe 8 of ours, the rest have weird names like 'android-7f2a' and 'ESP_123456' and it's freaking me out a bit

my neighbor asked for the wifi password yesterday and now i'm paranoid, is there a way to see every single device on the network? i want to make sure its just our phones and laptops and the smart tv not some random person
heard changing dns can make websites load faster, something about google dns or cloudflare? my friend said to use 1.1.1.1 but i have no idea where to even put those numbers in the settings

so my son says we should switch to opendns for parental controls or something, but when i go into the router settings there's like three different places for dns numbers and i dont want to break anything

websites were working fine this morning but now half of them say 'server not found' or take forever to load, my coworker said something about flushing dns cache? does that mean clearing browser history or is it different

ok this is weird, i can go to google.com fine but when i type in my work's vpn portal it says it can't find the server, but my coworker says it works for them. someone mentioned dns cache being stale? how do i clear that thing
which dns am i even using right now? my isp's or something else? i tried looking in network settings but it just says 'automatic' and that doesnt tell me anything useful

my desktop is plugged in with a cable but the little light on the port isnt blinking like it usually does, and the internet is super slow. is the cable bad? the port broken? how do i even check if its actually connected properly

so i ran a new ethernet cable through the wall to my office and now the connection keeps dropping, the lights on the router port go on and off. did i crimp the ends wrong? is there a way to test if the link is actually good
is the firewall thing on? i never turned it on but my friend said linux has one built in called ufw? i dont want people getting into my computer from the wifi at the coffee shop when i work there
my antivirus popped up saying the firewall is disabled, but i'm pretty sure i never messed with it. how do i check if its actually running or if something turned it off?

need to set up a guest wifi for when my parents visit so they dont have access to my main network with all my files and the printer. the router app has a guest network toggle but it asks for a separate password and i'm not sure if that's actually secure enough

running a small bakery from home and customers ask for wifi, but i dont want them on the same network as my square reader and inventory laptop. how do i make a separate guest thing that actually keeps them separated?

where do i find the mac address? the it guy at work needs it to let my laptop on the corporate wifi, but everything i google shows different names for it like 'hardware address' or 'physical address' and i see like 5 different ones in settings
my company's vpn requires registering the mac address but i have no clue which one is the right one - there's wifi, ethernet, bluetooth, and some virtual ones. which one do they actually need?
what's my ip address? not the public one the one that starts with 192.168 i think? i'm trying to set up a pi-hole and it's asking for the server ip

trying to access my router settings page and it says to go to 192.168.1.1 but that doesn't work. how do i find the actual address? my friend said it might be 192.168.0.1 or 10.0.0.1 but i dont want to guess

nothing loads at all, not even google. the wifi icon says connected but browser just spins forever. phone works fine on same wifi so its not the router. already restarted the computer twice. what else could it be

zoom keeps freezing and people say i'm robot-voice, and my games have crazy lag spikes. ran a speed test and it says 200 down but something feels off. how do i check if packets are getting lost or something?

need to forward a port for my security cameras so i can check them from work. the app says port 8080 but the router page has like 5 different port forwarding sections and i'm scared i'll open something i shouldn't
